drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: We have expanded the draft to address Buyer’s requested protections, subject to our client’s review and approval and agreement on the outstanding commercial particulars. We propose a cash-free, debt-free completion-accounts mechanism, a 10% escrow for 12 months, and proportionate warranty and indemnity limitations, with no contractual limitation for fraud. Diligence should be completed before signing rather than remain a discretionary closing condition. Please provide your proposed disclosure requests and confirm the target, share particulars, headline price, working-capital target and governing law so that the schedules and remaining blanks can be settled.

edits.text: PARTIES AND DEFINITIONS. This Agreement is between [Seller’s full legal name] (Seller) and Meridian Acquisitions LLC (Buyer). Company means [target’s full legal name and jurisdiction]. Shares means all issued and outstanding shares of the Company, comprising [number and class], as specified in Schedule 1. Base Purchase Price means USD [agreed amount]. Purchase Price means the Base Purchase Price, plus Closing Cash, less Closing Debt and unpaid Company transaction expenses, and plus or minus the amount by which Closing Working Capital exceeds or falls short of the agreed target of USD [amount], without double counting. The definitions, accounting policies and illustrative calculation in Schedule 2 must be agreed before signing.
edits.name: Parties and transaction definitions

edits.text: 1. SALE AND PURCHASE PRICE. At Closing, Seller shall transfer the Shares to Buyer free of encumbrances, against payment of the Purchase Price. Seller shall deliver a good-faith estimated completion statement at least five business days before Closing. Buyer shall pay the estimated Purchase Price at Closing, less the Escrow Amount. Within 60 days after Closing, Buyer shall deliver completion accounts prepared in accordance with Schedule 2, applying the agreed accounting policies consistently and excluding purchase-accounting adjustments and effects of Buyer’s post-Closing actions. Seller shall have access to relevant records and personnel and 30 days to object with reasonable particulars. Undisputed items shall be final. Unresolved accounting items shall be referred to an independent accountant jointly appointed by the parties, acting as expert and confined to the disputed items and the parties’ submitted positions. Fees shall be allocated by relative success. Any resulting payment shall be made within five business days after final determination. The adjustment process shall not permit double recovery under any other provision.
edits.name: Completion accounts

edits.text: 2. INTERIM PERIOD, CLOSING AND TERMINATION. The parties shall aim to Close within thirty days after signing, and in any event within five business days after satisfaction or waiver of the applicable conditions. Closing is conditional on required regulatory approvals and scheduled material third-party consents, no law or order prohibiting Closing, each party’s material performance of its obligations, and the other party’s warranties being accurate at Closing, disregarding inaccuracies that would not materially impair that party’s ability to complete or, for Seller’s business warranties, materially adversely affect the Company as a whole. Buyer shall complete satisfactory due diligence before signing; there shall be no post-signing discretionary diligence or financing condition. Pending Closing, Seller shall cause the Company to operate in the ordinary course, preserve its business and maintain its records, and shall not issue securities, make distributions, incur material non-ordinary-course debt, dispose of material assets or enter material non-ordinary-course commitments without Buyer’s consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. Exceptions shall apply for disclosed matters, applicable law and reasonably necessary emergency actions with prompt notice. Buyer shall receive reasonable access subject to confidentiality, privilege, competition law and non-disruption safeguards. Closing deliveries shall include share transfers, certificates or equivalent title evidence, required corporate approvals and agreed releases of encumbrances, against payment. Either party may terminate by written notice if Closing has not occurred within 90 days after signing, unless its own breach caused the failure; if a final non-appealable prohibition prevents Closing; or for the other party’s material breach preventing satisfaction of a closing condition that remains uncured for 20 business days after notice. Termination shall not affect accrued liability for prior breach, and confidentiality and dispute provisions shall survive.
edits.name: Closing protections and termination

edits.text: 3. WARRANTIES. Seller warrants at signing and Closing, subject to matters fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope in the agreed disclosure schedules, that: (a) Seller owns the Shares free of encumbrances and has capacity and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement; (b) the Shares constitute all issued share capital of the Company and there are no undisclosed rights to acquire securities; (c) the Company is duly organized and validly existing; (d) the scheduled financial statements fairly present in all material respects the Company’s financial position and results under the identified accounting standards, subject, for interim accounts, to normal year-end adjustments and absence of notes; (e) all material tax returns have been timely filed and are materially accurate, all material taxes due have been paid or adequately provided for, and no material tax dispute is pending or, to Seller’s knowledge, threatened in writing; (f) no material litigation is pending or, to Seller’s knowledge, threatened in writing against the Company; and (g) the Company has no material liabilities except those reflected or reserved in the financial statements, fairly disclosed in the schedules, or incurred in the ordinary course since the accounts date. Seller’s knowledge means the actual knowledge, after reasonable inquiry of their direct reports, of the individuals identified in Schedule 3. Buyer warrants its organization, authority, enforceability of its obligations and availability at Closing of sufficient immediately available funds. No warranty is given as to forecasts or future performance. The parties shall agree and attach the disclosure schedules before signing.
edits.name: Seller and Buyer warranties

edits.text: 4. INDEMNIFICATION, ESCROW AND GENERAL TERMS. Seller shall indemnify Buyer for actual losses resulting from breach of Seller’s warranties or covenants and for Company taxes attributable to pre-Closing periods, except to the extent reflected in the final Purchase Price. Buyer shall indemnify Seller for losses resulting from Buyer’s breaches. Claims must be notified with reasonable particulars before the applicable survival period expires; timely notified claims survive until resolved. General warranties survive for 18 months after Closing; title, capitalization and authority warranties survive for six years; tax warranties and the pre-Closing tax indemnity survive until 60 days after the applicable statutory limitation period. Covenants survive for their stated terms or, if none, the applicable limitation period. General warranty claims are subject to a deductible basket of 0.5% of the final Purchase Price and an aggregate cap of 10% of that price. Seller’s aggregate liability for title, capitalization, authority and tax claims shall not exceed the final Purchase Price; claims under interim operating covenants shall also be subject to that aggregate cap. No contractual exclusion, cap, basket or survival limitation applies to fraud. Buyer shall withhold 10% of the estimated Purchase Price at Closing into an independent escrow under an agreed escrow agreement securing Seller’s indemnity obligations. The escrow shall be released 12 months after Closing, less reasonable amounts reserved for timely notified unresolved claims, with reserved amounts released promptly upon resolution. Escrow is security and does not expand liability. An indemnified party shall give prompt notice of a third-party claim; delay excuses liability only to the extent materially prejudicial. The indemnifying party may assume the defense with reasonably acceptable counsel upon acknowledging its indemnity obligation, but not where material non-monetary relief, criminal liability or a material conflict is involved. The indemnified party may participate at its own expense. No settlement may impose an admission, non-monetary obligation or payment on the indemnified party, or omit its full release, without its consent. The parties shall reasonably cooperate, mitigate recoverable losses and prevent double recovery; recoveries shall be reduced by insurance proceeds actually received, net of collection costs and resulting premium increases. Except for fraud, equitable relief and the completion-accounts mechanism, this clause provides the exclusive post-Closing remedy for matters covered by this Agreement. This Agreement and any non-contractual obligations arising from it shall be governed by Delaware law, excluding conflicts rules, with exclusive jurisdiction in the state courts of Delaware or, where federal jurisdiction exists, the federal courts located in Delaware. Amendments and waivers must be in writing signed by the affected parties. Neither party may assign this Agreement without the other’s written consent; Buyer may assign to an affiliate without release of Buyer’s obligations. This Agreement, its schedules and the escrow agreement constitute the entire agreement concerning the transaction; nothing excludes liability for fraud.
edits.name: Indemnity framework and general provisions

partner.private_reasoning: The rendered agreement and cover note do not disclose the Executive’s confidential minimum severance or refer to that negotiating position. No hidden-content categories are identified in the supplied package.

receiver.message_back: Buyer can proceed on the cash-free, debt-free completion-accounts framework, pre-signing diligence and Delaware law, provided general-warranty protection is increased to a 20% cap with a 0.5% tipping basket and the 10% escrow remains for the full 18-month warranty period; we also require warranties covering material contracts, legal compliance, IP, employment and benefits, and no material adverse change, with fundamental warranties accurate in all respects at Closing. Please provide corresponding disclosure schedules, the fully diluted capitalization and title records, financial statements and proposed completion-account policies, tax filings and audits, material contracts and consent requirements, litigation and compliance records, IP ownership records and employee/benefit liabilities; target identity, share particulars, headline price and working-capital target remain subject to our client’s confirmation, and no agreement is binding until execution.

The Buyer shall pay the Seller the Purchase Price for the Shares. 2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur within thirty days of signing. 3. REPRESENTATIONS.
